transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-12-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO - HelioGrid), Eric Zhang (ML Eng), Sofia Martinez (PM)

Summary:
Quick scouting call to understand HelioGrid's inference needs: large context for long conversation history and telemetry, multilingual support (EN/ES/JP/BR-PT), tool-calling to internal ticketing & billing systems, and decision criteria for hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC. Discussed open-model candidates, context-length tradeoffs and initial benchmark plan.

Topics:
- current stack and constraints (AWS, internal VPC, compliance)
- target latency and cost envelope
- context length (up to ~256k tokens claimed, verifying)
- multilingual performance priorities
- tool-calling and RAG architecture
- pilot scope and next steps

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: all right good afternoon everyone, thanks for taking the time. this is maya from Redwood, our se liam is on as well, and we wanted to hear more about HelioGrid's plans and use cases.
[00:12] Priya: hi yeah thanks, we appreciate it. i'm priya, cto. short context — HelioGrid runs a customer support platform for IoT energy devices, lots of long-running conversations, we want an assistant that can reason over months of history and call internal tools.
[00:26] Liam: awesome, can you say roughly how much history? like avg conversation length, or total tokens you expect to pass in?
[00:34] Eric: so there's two patterns — realtime support threads are 2–5k tokens usually, but for diagnosis we want a concat of device telemetry + prior tickets which could be 40–100k tokens. for some escalations we think 150–200k might be useful, depending on pruning.
[00:50] Maya: okay so large context is a clear requirement, noted. are you thinking about fine-tuning or few-shot prompting with retrieval?
[00:59] Sofia: primarily RAG + tool-calling. we need the model to call internal ticket API, run a search over vector DB, and optionally write back a triage note. also language: english + spanish + portuguese + japanese for a subset.
[01:12] Liam: got it. so a few dimensions to consider: model family (some open models support long context better), hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated GPU vs private vpc), and whether quantization affects your tool-calling reliability.
[01:24] Priya: we have compliance constraints — customer PII can't leave our VPC for many accounts; we'll need either Redwood Private or Dedicated with strict data controls. SOC2 type II is baseline, plus KMS integration, audit logs.
[01:38] Maya: yep that's in line with other enterprise asks. we support SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments, and detailed audit logs. we'll share the SOC2 and network diagram docs after the call.
[01:48] Priya: perfect. one question on models — our team looked at Llama-2-chat, Mistral-Instruct, Falcon-40B, and a couple of 70b variants. curious how Redwood recommends across latency and cost for these workloads.
[02:01] Liam: right. quick high-level: Falcon-40B and Mistral-Instruct variants tend to be cost-effective and good for instruction following; Llama-2-chat family has good chat safety tuning. but critical for you is context length — many models are limited to 32k or 64k natively, whereas Redwood has pathways for extended context via 2-stage RAG and specialized long-context kernels. we also have Redwood-verified perf profiles for each model so you can see tokens/sec and tail latencies.
[02:26] Eric: when you say extended context via kernels, do you mean you stitch kv caches or use chunked attention? some of our folks mentioned "k-v cash" earlier in notes — sorry, k-v cache.
[02:36] Liam: yeah, there are a few approaches. for autoregressive models we manage KV cache and attention window optimizations at the runtime level, and we can do progressive chunking for retrieval-fusion. it's not magic — there are cost/latency tradeoffs. for true 100k+ contexts we'd typically do retrieval + re-ranking and only push condensed context to the main model, or use specialized long-context variants if available.
[02:56] Priya: what about latency SLOs? we need top-level agent suggestions in under 800ms median for realtime replies, but for deep diagnostics we're okay with 2–4s if it's a heavier step.
[03:07] Maya: that's reasonable. hosted mode tends to give fastest onboarding but less isolation; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can reserve capacity for lower p99 spikes. Private deployment can meet your VPC requirements but will require more setup and network config.
[03:20] Sofia: curious about tool-calling reliability — if model is quantized to int8, does it still call our APIs correctly? we've seen hallucinations in previous tests.
[03:28] Liam: quantization can slightly change tokenization boundaries and probability mass which affects exact slot filling, so we recommend test passes. Redwood Optimize has quantization profiles tuned per model and a test harness for function-calling / tool reliability. we'll run those as part of the pilot.
[03:44] Eric: any differences across models for multilingual? we have a lot of spanish and brazilian portuguese in support.
[03:50] Liam: Mistral and Falcon have decent multilingual abilities but model-specific; Llama family with instruction‑tuning can be good too. for production we often do per-language evals and tune retrieval to include language-matched context. we can share per-model language eval spreadsheets.
[04:05] Priya: regarding pricing, is there a per-token hosted cost and a flat monthly for Dedicated?
[04:10] Maya: yes hosted is per-token with tiers; Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit) with lower per-token unit economics once reserved. Private has platform fee + infra. i'll attach the cost sheet after call.
[04:20] Sofia: timeline — we want a pilot by mid-jan. final decision end of q1. is that workable?
[04:26] Maya: absolutely. typical pilot roadmap: 2–4 week integration to vet RAG + tool calls, run bench marks, then extend or move to dedicated.
[04:34] Priya: for pilot we'll want to run our real logs — can you run benchmarks against customer data in a dedicated sandbox?
[04:41] Liam: yes, we can set up a dedicated test namespace or run on-redwood hosted sandboxes depending on your data residency. for sensitive accounts we'd recommend dedicated or private.
[04:50] Eric: can you clarify "test namespace" — do you mean a dedicated deployment in Redwood Dedicated or a private VPC?
[04:56] Liam: both are options. dedicated pools mean our infra runs a private GPU pool for you in our environment; private means we ship a control plane into your VPC and inference runs in your network. each has different onboarding friction.
[05:08] Maya: quick note — we've seen customers combine approach: short-term pilot on hosted with synthetic/anonymized samples, parallel dedicated benchmark for realistic latency/cost results.
[05:18] Sofia: ok makes sense. a couple more technical Qs: 1) do you support streaming token responses with intermediate tool calls? 2) can models call external tools mid-generation?
[05:26] Liam: we have streaming and function/tool calling primitives. typical pattern: model emits a tool-call action; runtime interrupts and executes the tool, feeds results back, and resumes generation. streaming around tool calls is supported but the UX is a bit more complex. we'll demo that in the next session.
[05:42] Priya: any gotchas around rate limits and batching? our traffic is bursty when firmware rolls outs hit support.
[05:49] Maya: we provide quota controls and autoscaling/burst policies on Dedicated. for bursty workloads, caching/prerendering and intelligent batching reduce cost. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching thresholds tuned to your latency SLOs.
[05:59] Eric: okay, last point — how do we evaluate model regressions? we have a set of golden prompts and requirements around not hallucinating billing amounts.
[06:07] Liam: we recommend adding evals into CI — Redwood has the eval harness and can run regression alerts on model updates. you can pin models per-route to avoid surprises.
[06:18] Priya: great. can you also include notes on encryption at rest and in transit? our security team will want specifics on KMS and HSM integrations.
[06:26] Maya: yes we will share a security pack that includes KMS options, key rotation, and audit log samples.
[06:33] Priya: ok thanks.
[06:34] Maya: to recap next steps quickly — maya will send cost sheet, SOC2 and network docs; liam will run a 64k/64k-ish context throughput test on two candidate models and propose pilot configs; eric will share sample logs. we'll schedule the bench deep-dive for week of 2027-12-13.
[06:52] Sofia: sounds good, thanks.
[06:54] Priya: thanks everyone.
[06:55] Maya: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invites and the links.
